doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: The word "gig"
summary: Monk and Hal discuss the term gig versus job among jazz players.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: I see. I wanted to wrap up just with an observation that I’ve been noticing and that is what used to be our word, and I’m speaking of “gig” — has now become usurped in a number of ways. I remember hearing DJs start talking about, “I have a gig tomorrow.” And I remember being like don’t say that, you don’t have a gig. And now we have the gig economy which further usurps our own word.

But Monk, I remember when I was still working the guys would always say, “I’ve got this gig” at so-and-so. Especially the jazz players. “I’ve got a gig at Donte’s” or at the Lighthouse. Occasionally it would be a “job.” Job is more formal. A gig was, the guys would say that among themselves. So that terminology has been around a long time in the big cities, and the outlying areas may not have picked that up as fast, but it’s been around a long time.
